summary: Continued from a prior compaction already mid-DLSS-NR work. Closed out and shipped three separate pieces: (1) feat/dlssnr-upscale-method-toggle (SGSR1 edge threshold retuned to 0.3 default from user's own in-game finding) -> PR #9 -> v0.1.1. (2) feat/dlssnr-sgsr1-vulkan (Vulkan port of the SGSR1 reduced-resolution enlarge pass, code-complete and build-verified but explicitly NOT in-game verified on Vulkan) -> PR #10 -> v0.1.2, shipped untested per user's explicit choice, release notes disclosed the gap. (3) docs/readme-housekeeping (wrong-fork links, missing wilsjo2 attribution) -> PR #11, merged. Then diagnosed and fixed a genuinely new bug: vertical-line artifacts under Apply-before-SR + reduced model resolution. Four fix attempts before finding the real cause -- three rounds smoothing the resolve's gSource/gModel enlarge read (tap spacing, then a real gModelWorkScale-vs-actual-buffer-size bug) all produced zero visible change, confirmed via a diagnostic log that the code was genuinely executing. Root cause turned out to be Replace mode's NeutwoDecode/HybridDecode having no highlight guard at all by design, diverging near white; fixed by reapplying the existing Highlight-guard/gMaxRatio clamp to Replace's result, confirmed removing the artifact on the user's own hardware (Dawnwalker). Also found and fixed (then reverted at user's request, keeping scope to the guard alone) a real white-point/exposure bug: 'Game exposure' source silently fell back to static paper-white for games supplying DLSS.Pre.Exposure without an ExposureTexture. Shipped as PR #12 (2 commits -- the fix, then 3 real bugs caught by the project's own code-review skill: a degenerate near-black decode the guard's multiplicative rescale couldn't pull back up, the guard running before detail injection could widen past it, a stale menu tooltip) -> v0.1.3. Then, per direct user request, created a new AI-OS skill (EP-4, core.ux-review.sk / UX_REVIEW) distilling universal UI/UX heuristics filtered to this project's actual surface (the ImGui overlay), after first surfacing and ruling out a narrower reading (EVOLVE_BENCHMARK, explicitly scoped to the framework's own dev repo, not this installed project). Ran MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE to close this out: archived 2 fully-closed task files (feat_dlssnr-upscale-method-toggle, fix_dlssnr-presr-reduced-res-aliasing -- sgsr1-vulkan's task file left open, still genuinely awaiting in-game verification), confirmed via  that several years-old still-open-looking status notes in the rolling main.md task file (PR #2 jitter-cancel, PR #5 hybrid re-port, PR #6 AC1+CSP) are actually long since merged and stale; deeper promotion of main.md's older technical backlog (the DLSS-NR jitter investigation) deliberately deferred rather than rushed under time pressure -- left as-is per the framework's own 'don't force a promotion' rule.
next_up: feat_dlssnr-sgsr1-vulkan task file still open pending real in-game Vulkan verification. main.md's older backlog (jitter investigation, AC1+CSP/PR#2/PR#5 status lines now confirmed stale) still needs a proper drain pass -- next MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE should verify the jitter finding against current DlssNr_DeferredSr.inl content (it now has jitter-related code that didn't exist when the original note was written) before promoting or discarding it, and strip the now-confirmed-stale PR status lines. neural-manhwa-restyle epic (memory/plans/2026-09-09-neural-manhwa-restyle.md) still approved, not started. feat_dlssnr-detail-transfer and dlss-neural-rendering branch task files untouched this session, not reviewed.

summary: Ran UX_REVIEW against DlssNr_Menu.cpp (full-menu scope narrowed to the DLSS-NR panel), then a follow-up naming-only pass, surfacing 8 findings: a Highlight-guard slider range silently jumping from 8x to 30x when an unrelated 'Lift model pass limit' toggle was on, 5 missing Reset buttons, and naming issues (an internal 'Neutwo' codename leaking into the visible HDR-mapping dropdown, inconsistent Super Resolution/SR abbreviation, an undefined NVIDIA FG abbreviation). Planned and executed the fix (menu-ux-polish plan, 8/8), then a second plan added a user-specified 'Optimized Defaults' preset button (~25 fields, a total-pixel-count-based Model-resolution branch, an exposure-dependent Highlight guard) after three rounds of AskUserQuestion pinned down real edge-case ambiguities (ultrawide resolution comparison basis, no-active-feature fallback, preset scope). Both plans built on one branch (fix/dlssnr-nr-menu-ux) per user's explicit choice. User then asked to 'prepare for release': investigation found v0.1.3 (PR #12) was already a published GitHub Release -- an initial claim that it was never tagged was WRONG (based on local git tags only, not `gh release list`) and had to be corrected before acting on it. Learned this fork's real release mechanism: a workflow_dispatch GitHub Actions job (package_release.yml) builds+packages on a hosted runner, uploaded as a build artifact, then a human/agent publishes it as a GitHub Release with `gh release create`. Committed both plans as one commit (interleaved edits, not worth a risky hunk-level split), opened PR #13, merged it per explicit user go-ahead (no external review pause), triggered the release workflow -- then the user asked to cancel it mid-build ('remove the last release', clarified via AskUserQuestion to mean the in-flight v0.1.4 build, not the existing v0.1.3). Cancelled cleanly; confirmed no tag/release had been created yet. User then reported the Model-resolution slider silently stopped taking effect -- root-caused to PR #13's own Reset button becoming ImGui's new 'last item', breaking a IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit()-based deferred-commit check further down; fixed and opened as PR #14. Ran the code-review skill against PR #13/#14, which found two more real issues (Highlight guard's UI cap didn't clamp the underlying DlssNrMaxRatio value at 2 of 4 shader call sites; ApplyOptimizedDefaults duplicated an exposure-check ternary) -- both independently verified against the cited file:line before fixing, then pushed to PR #14. User completed in-game testing themselves, then authorized merge + release; PR #14 merged, package_release.yml re-run to completion, tagged and published as v0.1.4-optimized-defaults. Ran TASK_CLOSE on fix_dlssnr-nr-menu-ux: promoted 2 verified truths to semantic memory (known_gotchas.md: the IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit 'last submitted item' gotcha; conventions_patterns.md: config values with a semantic ceiling need clamping at every consumer, not just the UI slider's range), archived the task file. gh pr edit hit a repo-specific GraphQL bug (deprecated Projects-classic field) on this repo regardless of content -- worked around via `gh api ... -X PATCH` directly.

summary: Continued the KleberMotta MFG unlock port. Re-applied it on wilsjo2 v0.8.4 as a clean compile-flag branch and opened PR #79 (PR #78 from our main was closed). Testing on the user RTX 5070 Ti in Cyberpunk exposed a freeze on that line with OptiFG (FSR FG) and NR on; the unlock was not involved (Blackwell, no MFG unlock log lines). Found the cause with live thread stacks and a linker-map build: State::ApplyToFinishedPicture called GetBuffer on the FG swapchain under the NR mutexes before checking Finished Picture, deadlocking with the FSR FG present thread. The main-line function has the gate from e237f895; the v0.8.4 rewrite c16a98e7 dropped it. Fixed as PR #80 (7a055d40, 10 lines), confirmed by the user in game (2295/2295 FG presents). Also built and handed over three separate test builds (main, kleber port, v0.8.4 plus fix) and did the clang-format pass. Session and clock times were not recorded, so started/ended are date only.
